passages.provision_quote: A public school, school district or state agency or an employee of a public school, school district or state agency may not provide or allow any person to provide instruction to students or employees that promotes or advocates for any of the following concepts:
passages.note: Senate engrossed text prints the operative prohibition and its civil-penalty and certificate-discipline enforcement, but names no voter.

rows.reasoning: Mesnard prime-sponsored SB 1305 (2023), "race; ethnicity; prohibited instruction", and voted Y on its third reading; its operative section says a school "may not provide or allow any person to provide instruction to students or employees that promotes or advocates for any of the following concepts", a list of seven race and ethnicity propositions, enforced by civil penalties and teacher discipline on complaint by a student, employee or parent. That is the rung that would "Prohibit lessons on race, gender, or sexuality that the community considers divisive or age-inappropriate". It is not the rung that would "Keep the curriculum focused on core academics and leave contested social topics to families", because subsection G expressly preserves instruction "identifying and discussing historical movements, ideologies or instances of racial hatred or discrimination, including slavery, Indian removal, the holocaust and Japanese-American internment" rather than removing those topics from school.
